title: Weekly arXiv physics: 7–13 November 2026 — notable recent papers
global_caveat: ArXiv supplies no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from checkable publication, coverage, cross-list, artifact and result signals. Citation evidence is limited for papers this new, so the ranking is not a measured popularity list.

sections.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
sections.abstract: The authors use a differentiable physical model to subtract starlight from JWST/NIRCam coronagraph data, reporting 2–15× better sensitivity than standard methods and a first 4.3 μm image of 51 Eridani b.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 2–15× sensitivity improvements on JWST/NIRCam data and an SNR 6.3 detection of 51 Eridani b in the 4.3 μm filter.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; tested on observational JWST/NIRCam coronagraph data.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors have not reached the photon-noise limit and say their model is not yet systematically calibrated to infer instrument-instability parameters with uncertainties.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Published in Nature; independent Caltech coverage; demonstrated on real JWST observations with a reported previously unavailable planet detection.

sections.title: Intracycle Interference in Strong-Field Photoemission from a Tungsten Needle Tip
sections.abstract: Carrier-envelope-phase-resolved spectra from a tungsten needle driven at 1570 nm reveal intracycle interference among rescattered plateau electrons, supported by quantum-orbit and time-dependent Schrödinger-equation simulations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify intracycle interference near the rescattering cutoff in two-cycle, CEP-stable photoemission spectra and use the pattern to probe electron dynamics on attosecond timescales.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; carrier-envelope-phase-resolved photoemission from a nanometric tungsten tip, interpreted with quantum-orbit and TDSE simulations.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors suggest electronic decoherence may explain the lack of clear interference at lower energies; that interpretation is not itself a direct measurement of the decoherence mechanism.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Published in Physical Review Letters; reports a first experimental observation of this interference in plateau electrons and has an associated public data/figure package.

sections.title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
sections.abstract: The authors report a halide pretreatment that strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite cells, reaching 26.9% certified efficiency and retaining 94% of initial efficiency after 400 thermal cycles from −40 to 85 °C.
sections.claimed_result: The authors attribute improved adhesion and cycling tolerance to hierarchical interfacial anchoring, with device efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and 94% retention after 400 cycles.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; inverted perovskite solar-cell fabrication, efficiency certification and thermal cycling.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported cycling protocol is a laboratory stress test; it does not by itself establish field lifetime under the full range of operating and degradation conditions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper has a Science Advances DOI and reports certified device efficiency and a concrete thermal-cycling test, connecting materials chemistry to device durability.

sections.title: Nucleon sigma terms in lattice QCD at physical pion mass and in the continuum
sections.abstract: Using four physical-pion-mass lattice ensembles at four lattice spacings, the authors extract continuum light, strange and charm nucleon sigma terms while fitting contributions from low-lying multihadron excited states.
sections.claimed_result: The authors obtain σπN = 53.0(7.4)(1.6) MeV, σs = 58.2(17.0)(2.1) MeV and σc = 112(28)(25) MeV, quoting statistical and systematic uncertainties.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; Nf=2+1+1 twisted-mass lattice-QCD ensembles and global continuum fits.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported errors remain sizable, particularly for σs and σc; the extraction also depends on modeling multihadron excited-state contributions and continuum behavior.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across four high-energy and nuclear subfields; combines physical-mass ensembles, four lattice spacings and explicit excited-state treatment, with relevance to dark-matter scattering inputs.

sections.title: Supercurrent-controlled magnon transport via suppression of the superconducting gap
sections.abstract: In a ferromagnet/superconductor heterostructure, the authors observe declining magnon transport as supercurrent rises and attribute it to gap suppression that increases dissipation into Bogoliubov quasiparticles.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report direct experimental evidence that supercurrent suppresses magnon transport through enhanced quasiparticle dissipation in the superconducting layer.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; magnon-transport measurements in a ferromagnet/superconductor heterostructure.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is demonstrated in a specific heterostructure; transferability and operating range for other magnonic devices remain to be established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted for publication in Physical Review Applied; experiment links supercurrent, superconducting-gap changes and magnon transport without relying on Joule heating.

sections.title: UniHam: A Large-Scale SOC-Complete Dataset and Benchmark for Hamiltonian Learning in Materials
sections.abstract: UniHam provides more than 100,000 DFT-computed, spin-orbit-coupled Hamiltonians spanning 72 elements and benchmarks learned Hamiltonians for reconstruction, out-of-distribution generalization and downstream properties.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find element- and SOC-dependent failure modes, variable compositional OOD robustness, and a need for spectral-level evaluation before Hamiltonian predictions are trusted for downstream properties.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; DFT-generated Hamiltonian dataset and machine-learning benchmark.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark is built from DFT-computed Hamiltonians; its results do not alone validate predictions against measured material behavior.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: KDD 2026 proceedings paper; the benchmark addresses a stated data gap and tests model behavior under composition and symmetry shifts.

sections.title: MAGI (Multivariate Autoencoder for particle Generative Inference): a generative Machine Learning framework for accelerated multi-stage particle simulations
sections.abstract: MAGI learns particle crossings with a conditional variational autoencoder and, in benchmark Geant4 simulations, reports detector-level rates consistent with full simulation at about 1σ while accelerating some cases by nearly 240×.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report statistical amplification from 150 to 12,000 and computational speedups from 2.1× to almost 240×, depending on source and mass model.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; conditional-VAE resampling validated against Geant4 detector-level simulations.
sections.unique_caveat: Validation is on benchmark models within the same Geant4 simulation framework; accuracy and speedup may vary with geometry, source and simulation configuration.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed between astrophysical instrumentation and particle experiment; Zenodo software release and comparison against full Geant4 results.

sections.title: Impact of dynamical, quadratic, and higher-order tidal effects on gravitational-wave observations of binary neutron stars
sections.abstract: The authors incorporate dynamical and nonlinear tidal terms through 8PN order into neutron-star inspiral waveforms and use Bayesian comparisons to estimate when these terms could be distinguished or bias inferred tidal deformabilities.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that 8PN tidal response can rival lower-order terms for subsolar-mass systems and project that exceptionally loud GW170817-like events could resolve higher-order effects with third-generation detectors.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; post-Newtonian waveform modeling and Bayesian model comparisons, including Einstein Telescope projections.
sections.unique_caveat: The detector forecasts are conditional on unusually loud signals and assumed waveform/noise models; this is not a detection of an additional tidal effect.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across astrophysics, relativity, phenomenology and nuclear theory; quantifies a waveform-modeling effect relevant to future precision inference of dense nuclear matter.

sections.title: Quantum Computing Enhanced Search for Wavelike Dark Matter
sections.abstract: The authors propose a Grover-search-based quantum sensing strategy for weak axion signals and report projected sensitivity beyond astrophysical limits in a transmon-based benchmark, reaching the QCD axion band only in a scenario with one million entangled sensing qubits.
sections.claimed_result: The authors project access to axion parameter space beyond existing astrophysical limits and to the QCD axion band at the stated million-entangled-qubit scale.
sections.evidence_type: Forecast/proposal; quantum-algorithm analysis and transmon-based sensitivity benchmark, not an experimental dark-matter observation.
sections.unique_caveat: The projected reach depends on very large entangled-qubit resources and favorable sensing/coherence assumptions; the abstract does not demonstrate that scale in hardware.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across particle phenomenology, cosmology, experiment and quantum physics; develops a concrete sensing protocol with a transmon-based resource benchmark.
